localChanges: BridgeVersion 1.0.8 -> 1.0.9, and health now answers "template_library":true so the plugin can tell a build that serves the import from one that answers 404. Health is a hand-concatenated string, so a test reassembles its literals and parses them: the first 1.0.9 build dropped the quote that closed "invoke_session":"root" and a live Studio session answered invalid JSON, which fails every bridge call rather than only the import.

POST /bridge/library/import (ImportLibraryItemInline) plus its entry in _MutationRoutes: pulls one shipped template-library item and the types it depends on into the open project, calling TemplateLibrary.ImportLibraryItem inside Context.Sessions.ImpersonateRootTemporary() because a design-time method call without a session kills Studio with native heap corruption (the same root cause as node/invoke).

TypeConflictResolutionChoice and ConflictResolution are written as TemplateLibrary.TypeConflictResolutionChoice and TemplateLibrary.ConflictResolution: they are nested in TemplateLibrary, verified by compiling against UAManagedCore.dll 5.0.0.39. Only ConflictResolution.Replace is offered, because it is the only member the vendor documents.

ResolveDataType falls back to ResolveModuleTypeId, and ResolveModuleTypeId now scans each module's ObjectTypes AND VariableTypes catalogs: a module keeps its own type in ObjectTypes (DataLogger, Table, Trend) and the types of its children in VariableTypes (VariableToLog, StoreColumn, EventFieldPath, TrendPen), so scanning only ObjectTypes resolved every container and none of its contents. WriteVariableInline then puts a resolved module type in MakeVariable's variableType slot (dataType BaseDataType) instead of the dataType slot, refuses an ObjectType with a redirect to model/object, and takes an optional display_name query param. Builtin datatypes are untouched and still compile to the same NodeId.

POST /bridge/node/set-structured (SetStructuredInline and its helpers) plus its entry in _MutationRoutes: writes the element objects of one placeholder child collection (a trend's Pens, a store table's Columns, a DataLogger's VariablesToLog, an EventLogger's EventFieldPaths) from a JSON array body, effect append|replace, at most 200 items. The property is resolved from the node's declared CLR property and must be a PlaceholderChildNodeCollection, so it can never fabricate an undeclared variable (the crash the set_property array guard exists to prevent); elements are created through InformationModel.Make<T> by reflection (bare Activator.CreateInstance would make a detached proxy) and every field is written through GetVariable/the P*Variable accessor with CoerceAssign, so no coercion logic is duplicated. Everything is validated before the model changes, a failed batch rolls back the elements it created, and effect=replace reports that it cannot restore what it removed. No tool maps the route yet: the plugin's op vocabulary has set_property, not a structured write.

Upstream pull request against asqi-carter/ftx-mcp with the same verbs is still OPEN AS A TASK, not filed: filing it needs the upstream repository, so a later vendored release can drop these diffs once they land.
purpose: Design-time bridge loaded inside FactoryTalk Optix Studio; the native Node plugin does not run the upstream MCP or Python services.
